narration_timeline.text: Why is this little house sparrow throwing dry dirt all over its own feathers?
narration_timeline.scene: Actual house sparrow dust bathing in a flowerbed.

narration_timeline.text: It lowers its body into loose soil, then shakes and flutters in the dust.
narration_timeline.scene: House sparrow taking a dust bath in zoo grounds; explicitly captive setting.

narration_timeline.text: At the water's edge, another sparrow pauses while a different bird continues rubbing its feathers through dry earth.
narration_timeline.scene: A genuine zoo-ground dust bath contrasted with a separately filmed sparrow at water's edge; no unverified splash or same-animal continuity.

narration_timeline.text: Dust baths and water baths are two ways birds can care for their plumage.
narration_timeline.scene: House sparrow bathing in a bird bath; other species may be present.

narration_timeline.text: Between baths, a sparrow still spends its day searching plants and paths for food.
narration_timeline.scene: Female house sparrow visibly foraging among plants.

narration_timeline.text: After visiting dust or water, each sparrow continues its day, moving through the same busy search for food.
narration_timeline.scene: Separate authentic house-sparrow scenes, not one continuous individual returning from a bath.
